title: Move to Action: Turning Crucial Conversations Into Results
coreMove: Turn apparent agreement into accountable action by naming the decision mode and the follow-up owner.
sourcePressure: Conversation only becomes results when the group chooses an explicit decision method and closes with Who does What by When and Follow-up.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the close as productivity task management detached from dialogue.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

hook: dictionary definition of a crucial conversation
tryThisNow: pick a conversation and journal about it without a chapter-specific test
examples: manager feedback in a conference room
spouse argument at the kitchen counter
student raising hand in a classroom
generic two-hour meeting with no owner

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: regional food bank leadership team after debating freezer allocation for partner pantries
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations director closing a heated but constructive allocation debate
exampleSpecs.stakes: families lose fresh food if everyone leaves thinking someone else owns the new routing plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two weeks after alignment language, the director sees spoiled pallets and traces the miss to no named owner, deadline, or follow-up check
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A pallet of thawing spinach cases leaves a wet square on the warehouse floor.

exampleSpecs.domain: independent film crew deciding whether to cut a night shoot
exampleSpecs.audience: a line producer choosing command, consult, vote, or consensus under time pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: a bad decision either blows the budget or burns out the crew before the final location day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the producer states this is consult, gathers two inputs, then owns the decision instead of pretending the group will choose
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Wait," someone says, and a call sheet flaps under a sandbag beside a generator cable.

exampleSpecs.domain: dental practice partners choosing a new sterilization vendor
exampleSpecs.audience: a managing partner who needs buy-in but not universal preference
exampleSpecs.stakes: compliance continuity matters more than everyone loving the vendor
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the partner rejects default consensus, names vote as acceptable because all vetted vendors meet the standard, then assigns WWWF
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first signal is sensory before it is social: a sealed autoclave test strip packet sits on a pricing proposal.

exampleSpecs.domain: mountain guide service revising avalanche-course cancellation rules
exampleSpecs.audience: a head guide clarifying decision rights before winter bookings
exampleSpecs.stakes: ambiguous authority could put clients on unsafe terrain or anger them with late cancellations
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the guide says weather cancellations are command decisions, course-format changes are consult decisions, then writes who updates clients by what date
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You notice an avalanche beacon blinks beside a laminated route card before anyone names the problem.

exampleSpecs.domain: public radio pledge-drive team choosing which donor script to keep
exampleSpecs.audience: a campaign producer trying to move from debate to experiment
exampleSpecs.stakes: pledge revenue stalls if the group keeps reopening the same preference argument
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the producer names vote as wrong for a testable question, assigns one producer to A/B test two scripts by Friday, and schedules the follow-up readout
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Only later does the miss become obvious: two donor scripts are clipped to a studio music stand.

exampleSpecs.domain: veterinary clinic staff agreeing to change after-hours triage
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic manager making sure the agreement survives the first weekend
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients may be routed incorrectly if we will handle it remains the only owner
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager converts we should update triage into Mira changes the voicemail by Thursday noon and Felix audits Saturday calls Monday morning
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes when a voicemail script is taped beside the clinic phone cradle?

skillTargets: choose command, consult, vote, or consensus before the close
convert warm agreement into WWWF commitments
design follow-up that reveals non-action early

tryThisNowSpec: Take one open agreement and write four words under it: Who, What, When, Follow-up. Fill each with a name, a visible deliverable, a date, and the check that will prove it happened.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
